For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the plant milk base came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-plant-milk" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-plant-milk-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of plant milk base, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:plant-milk-d6b2742d4178:ad47fd9e367d"><summary>HMI plant milk base Pb reference · Plant milk base, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:plant-milk-d6b2742d4178:ad47fd9e367d"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI plant milk base Pb reference · Plant milk base, as sold. Plant milk base, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤1</td><td>1.9</td><td>1.9</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤1</td><td>1.9</td><td>1.9</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>3 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>FDA Total Diet Study</td><td>3</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for plant milk base, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach plant milk base

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach plant milk base comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Plant milk base, as sold from laboratory-prepared had lead higher at 53 µg/kg, against 6.8 µg/kg for laboratory-prepared in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Inna V. Begday, Tamara A. Tsesar, Konstantin V. Kharin · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Integral assessment of the environmental safety of plant-based milk alternatives based on heavy metal analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Izvestiya KGTU (KSTU News)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Inna V. Begday, Tamara A. Tsesar, Konstantin V. Kharin · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Integral assessment of the environmental safety of plant-based milk alternatives based on heavy metal analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Izvestiya KGTU (KSTU News)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing plant milk base for metals

<a id="hmi-ing-025"></a>
<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 1 µg/kg (FDA Total Diet Study) to 7 µg/kg (Zvěřina et al. 2025), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Plant milk base FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-plant-milk-base" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-plant-milk-base" data-question="What heavy metals are found in plant milk base?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in plant milk base?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury, nickel, chromium, uranium, Cu and Zn in plant milk base, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span Sandhu A, Jackson LS · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/redan2023-plant-milk-alternatives-elements">Analysis of Eight Types of Plant-based Milk Alternatives from the United States Market for Target Minerals and Trace Elements</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Composition and Analysis</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/redan2023-plant-milk-alternatives-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/zverina2025-plant-dairy-toxic-elements|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-plant-milk-base" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-plant-milk-base" data-question="How do heavy metals get into plant milk base?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into plant milk base?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, plant milk base from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than plant milk base from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Inna V. Begday, Tamara A. Tsesar, Konstantin V. Kharin · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Integral assessment of the environmental safety of plant-based milk alternatives based on heavy metal analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Izvestiya KGTU (KSTU News)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Plant milk base, as sold from laboratory-prepared had lead higher at 53 µg/kg, against 6.8 µg/kg for laboratory-prepared in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Inna V. Begday, Tamara A. Tsesar, Konstantin V. Kharin · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Integral assessment of the environmental safety of plant-based milk alternatives based on heavy metal analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Izvestiya KGTU (KSTU News)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/begday2026-plant-milk-heavy-metal-safety">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-plant-milk-base-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-plant-milk-base-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in plant milk base is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in plant milk base is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 1 result from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported inorganic arsenic in plant milk base, as sold from 40 results in 1 reporting region, with subgroup medians below 0.68 µg/kg, mostly non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
